original_question: Let f : Y -> B be a morphism from a smooth projective threefold to a smooth curve whose general fiber is a smooth surface. For a fixed geometric genus g, does there exist a constant b(Y,g) such that every vertical curve C subset Y of geometric genus g satisfies C^2 >= -b(Y,g), where the self-intersection is computed inside the fiber containing C?
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Problem 3.3.6: the question asking whether the very weak bounded negativity bound for fixed geometric genus extends from a single surface to a family of surfaces over a curve. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the ambient morphism f:Y->B from a smooth projective threefold to a smooth curve, the assumption that the general fibre is a smooth surface, the dependence of the bound only on Y and g, the restriction to vertical curves, and the instruction that C^2 be computed in the containing fibre. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
missing_details: The exact target is Problem 3.3.6, and it is introduced specifically as the family-extension of Conjecture 3.3.5 (Very weak bounded negativity), not as an unrelated threefold negativity problem. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
To match the paper exactly, the inequality is strict: C^2 > -b(Y,g), not C^2 >= -b(Y,g). ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
For a stand-alone formulation, vertical should be defined explicitly as f(C) being a point. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The nearby definition in Conjecture 3.3.4 makes clear that geometric genus means the genus of the normalization, so that should be spelled out if the question is to stand alone. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The genus parameter should be quantified as a fixed integer g>0, as in Conjectures 3.3.4 and 3.3.5. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The surrounding discussion is explicitly motivated by the failure of bounded negativity in positive characteristic (Example 3.3.3) and by the characteristic-zero formulations of Conjectures 3.3.4 and 3.3.5, so the intended context is the characteristic-zero weak/very weak bounded-negativity setting even though Problem 3.3.6 itself does not restate the characteristic. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
refined_question: In the characteristic-zero bounded-negativity setting of Section 3.3, let f:Y->B be a morphism from a smooth projective threefold to a smooth curve such that the general fibre is a smooth surface. Fix an integer g>0. Does there exist a constant b(Y,g)>0 such that every vertical curve C subset Y with f(C) a point and geometric genus g (i.e. the genus of the normalization of C) satisfies C^2 > -b(Y,g), where C^2 is computed in the fibre of f containing C? ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
justification: This is essentially Problem 3.3.6 almost verbatim. The draft already matches the morphism, the vertical-curve condition, the fixed geometric genus, and the fibrewise self-intersection. The refinements above only restore paper-specific context and precision: the problem is posed immediately after Conjectures 3.3.4 and 3.3.5 as a family version of very weak bounded negativity; Conjecture 3.3.4 supplies the meaning of geometric genus as genus of the normalization; and the surrounding discussion shows why the characteristic-zero setting is the intended one, via the positive-characteristic counterexample in Example 3.3.3. The paper does not give an explicit equivalent reformulation of Problem 3.3.6 nearby, so null is the faithful choice. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
